messages:
elaine: Heads up — linkcheck is failing on the PR that added the architecture diagrams. CI shows a bunch of anchor errors but only for images that go through a redirector (weird). Full log excerpt below.

elaine: ```
LinkCheckError: external link 'https://assets-cdn.company.com/redirect?u=https://s3.amazonaws.com/rdw-docs/diagrams#architecture' returned status 200 but anchor not found: '#architecture'
...
```

matt: can you paste the mkdocs/plugins section from the repo? want to repro locally. is this the mkdocs-link-checker plugin or the builtin linkcheck?

elaine: it's the mkdocs-link-checker plugin. mkdocs.yml excerpt: ```
plugins:
  - search
  - mkdocs-link-checker:
      check_anchors: true
      timeout: 10
      follow_redirects: false
```

priya: ahhh. follow_redirects=false will make the checker look only at the redirect response URL, which strips fragments. that explains the anchor mismatch. if the redirect response doesn't include the fragment we get this error.

matt: so we can either enable follow_redirects or special-case images served via the redirector. enabling redirects might mask other issues but seems correct for external image hosts. thoughts?

elaine: enabling follow_redirects seems simplest. are there any security reasons we avoid it? IIRC we turned it off because some internal redirectors returned 200 with a debug page occasionally and we wanted to flag it.

kevin: platform note — our CDN/redirector canonicalizes URLs and intentionally drops fragments on the redirect response. so link-checker following the redirect will end up hitting the S3 URL (which has the anchor) if follow_redirects=true. that's fine from a correctness POV.

priya: another option: add a linkcheck allowlist for the redirector host and skip anchor checks for those URLs. example: ```
link_checker_allowlist:
  - 'https://assets-cdn.company.com/redirect*'
```
But that's a bit of a band-aid.

matt: i'd prefer follow_redirects=true for now and add a small test. will open a tiny PR to flip the flag + add a job that runs linkcheck against one redirecting image.

elaine: if we flip it, please add a comment in the config explaining why so future folks don't flip it back. also add a short note in the PR description about the CDN behavior.

matt: will do. quick WIP: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2743 — changes: set follow_redirects: true, add linkcheck integration test, ignore-list example.

deploy-bot: CI started for matt/2743 (docs-linkcheck).

priya: small nit — can we only enable follow_redirects for external checks (not internal dev.local links)? the plugin doesn't support per-host rules AFAIK. but we could patch the plugin or run two passes: internal-only with strict flags, then external pass with follow_redirects. up to you.

kevin: running two passes in CI is reasonable: cheap and explicit. eng-infra could help if it becomes messy.

matt: i added a separate linkcheck job `linkcheck-external` that runs after build and only checks http(s) external links with follow_redirects=true. it uses the same plugin but a different mkdocs config file (mkdocs.linkcheck.external.yml).

elaine: perfect. can you also update docs/CONTRIBUTING.md to mention how to run the linkcheck locally (two commands)? saves a lot of time.

matt: added a brief note. PR updated.

docs-ci-bot: linkcheck-external job failed on first run: encountered a 429 from the redirector.

elaine: 429 = rate limit. that's the redirector's rate limiter kicking in. we shouldn't hammer it in CI. matt, can we cache the target S3 URL or use a single sample file instead of scanning every external image?

matt: changed the external job to only check known sample assets (one per host) to avoid rate limits. retesting.

deploy-bot: CI rerun for matt/2743 (linkcheck-external sample-only).

docs-ci-bot: ✅ linkcheck-external passed.

priya: thanks everyone. long-term we should consider adding a tiny HTTP client in the plugin that follows redirects but preserves fragment logic (i.e., if redirect response drops fragment, reapply from original). small PR welcome to the upstream plugin.

kevin: opened infra ticket to consider a staging mirror for docs assets so CI can hit a stable host without aux rate limits.

elaine: ok — looks green, sample-check passes, CONTRIBUTING updated. matt, can you merge when ready? i'll follow up to sweep the rest of the problematic image links and convert any that still point at the redirector to canonical S3/raw links where feasible. :thumbsup:

matt: merging now. thanks y'all :party_parrot:

kevin: FYI — i'll add a short note to the release checklist to include a docs linkcheck sanity step for PRs that add external assets.

elaine: awesome — thanks!
